To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
finite element analysis and genetic algorithms were successfully combined to design a composite vascular graft that exhibits a compliance of 6% /100 mmHg.
the combination of finite element models and genetic algorithms can be successfully used in the design of composite tissue engineering vascular grafts.

a composite graft design consisting of a porous polyurethane layer and a fabric layer with optimized mechanical properties can provide the required compliance of 6 %/100 mm Hg for a small diameter vascular graft.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a tissue regenerating vascular graft that combines a polyurethane-based scaffold for the regeneration of the vascular intimal and media layers, with a non-woven textile fabric for the regeneration of adventitia and the reinforcement of the composite graft.
the development of a novel vascular graft that combines the advantages of a biodegradable polyurethane with a fabric-reinforced adventitia.
the development of an optimal design of a modular tissue regenerative vascular prosthesis, which is based on a combination of finite element analysis and genetic algorithms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a fabric-reinforced porous graft with the mechanical properties of the adventitial fabric layer as predicted by the model and manufactured according to the predicted mechanical characteristics is able to achieve a diametric compliance in the range of native arteries.
the use of genetic algorithms and finite element models in combination with the experimental data is a powerful tool for the design and optimization of vascular grafts.
the use of genetic algorithms for optimization of the mechanical design of a composite graft was shown to be successful.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to develop a novel, modular vascular graft system with a compliance of 4% / 100 mmHgg, which is close to that of native vessels.
we were able to show the use of genetic algorithms and finite element methods to optimize the mechanical properties of a vascular graft.
the use of finite element methods in conjunction with genetic algorithms has been shown to be a powerful tool for the design of vascular grafts and other tissue engineering constructs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the design of a composite graft can be achieved by using a finite element analysis to predict the required mechanical properties of the individual layers and then use a genetic algorithm to optimize the mechanical design.
the combination of finite element modeling with genetic algorithms is a powerful tool for the design of vascular prostheses.
the use of finite element models and genetic algorithms is an effective way to optimize the mechanical design and the material selection for a composite graft.
